title: Insurance Premium Growth, Underwriting Risk, and Insurer Profitability: The Moderating Role of Reinsurance
content: This study analyzes the relationship among insurance premium growth, underwriting risk, and insurer profitability, while also examining the mediating role of underwriting risk and the moderating role of reinsurance. The panel dataset consists of 230 observations collected from the financial statements and annual reports of insurance companies. The study employs two-step System GMM to control for model dynamics, endogeneity, and unobserved firm-specific heterogeneity. The results show that underwriting risk is persistent over time, whereas insurance premium growth has no statistically significant effect on underwriting risk, ROA, or ROE. Underwriting risk also has no significant effect on profitability; therefore, its mediating role is not confirmed. Similarly, the interaction effect between premium growth and reinsurance is not statistically significant, providing no evidence of a moderating role for reinsurance. By contrast, the fixed asset ratio has a positive effect on both ROA and ROE, while ROE exhibits a negative adjustment pattern over time. The study indicates that premium growth alone is insufficient to improve profitability and highlights the importance of underwriting quality, efficient asset utilization, and risk management in insurance companies.
